requested.title: Admin gate is a raw-pathname prefix test decoupled from the route table
Framing protection exists only on the newsletter embed path, leaving /admin/ clickjackable
Admin panel is framable by any origin; one-click destructive POSTs defeat the Origin-based CSRF check
An empty CAPTCHA_MIN_AGE_MS silently sets the captcha timing floor to 0
MOCHI_KEY is load-bearing for captcha tokens but unenforced, and .env.example says otherwise
{{mochi.analytics}} placeholder is expanded against the assembled HTML, so user content can capture it
Public support-form submission has no rate limit — unbounded mail send and DB growth
purgeExpiredPendingSubscribers reads expired IDs outside its transaction and deletes unconditionally

Where F3 overstates relative to F2 is its central premise, asserted at 'high' confidence: 'the browser caches the credential per-origin and attaches it to *any* subsequent request to support.mochi.fast, including subresource/iframe loads'. That is pre-partitioning behaviour. The parsing bug is exactly as described and I confirmed every link. `Number('')` is `0` and `Number.isFinite(0)` is `true`, so `CAPTCHA_MIN_AGE_MS=` (or a whitespace-only value) resolves index.ts:56 to `minAgeMs: 0` instead of the intended 2000; `Number('abc')` is NaN and does fall back correctly, and the sibling `bits` on line 55 uses `||` so it is immune. `resolveCaptchaOptions` (captcha/config.ts:36-40) then takes it verbatim — `o.minAgeMs ?? DEFAULT` only replaces null/undefined, and the sole validation is `minAgeMs >= maxAgeMs`, which `0` passes — so there is no warning anywhere. `verifyCaptcha` (captcha/captcha.ts:95-102) applies the resolved value as the `ageMs < minAgeMs` floor, and config.ts:8-11 documents that floor as the only thing enforcing human-time submission since PoW solve time is geometrically distributed with no lower bound. The irony the finding points out is real: `authFailureDelay()` in adminAuth.ts:31-34 guards against this identical `Number('')` trap with an explicit comment, and index.ts does not copy it. I am downgrading severity because nothing in the committed configuration triggers it: `CAPTCHA_MIN_AGE_MS` is not mentioned in `.env.example` at all, so reaching `minAgeMs: 0` requires an operator to deliberately add the key with an empty value in the CapRover env. That makes it a latent config-parsing defect rather than a presently-weakened control — worth fixing (it compounds F7's missing rate limit on the same route), but not attacker-reachable as deployed.

Every link in this chain is verified. `mintCaptcha` seals the challenge with `encryptPayload(..., { aad: CAPTCHA_AAD })` (captcha/captcha.ts:51) and `verifyCaptcha` reopens it with `decryptPayload` (captcha.ts:66), returning `reject('malformed')` on `null`; `payloadCrypto.ts`'s `sivKey()` derives the AES-SIV key as `HMAC-SHA512(getMochiConfig().secretKey, …)`, and `initMochiConfig` (mochiConfig.ts:31-42) sets that secret from `MOCHI_KEY` or, when absent, from a per-boot `randomBytes(32)` behind nothing but a `logger.warn`. This app mints captchas on both of its public pages (routes.ts:36 and newsletter/routes.ts:23, each spread into `<MochiCaptcha>` via SupportForm.svelte:67), so the key is load-bearing here. Yet the `mochi:init` hook (index.ts:62-79) enforces only ADMIN_PASSWORD, SMTP_HOST and MOCHI_ORIGIN, and `.env.example` actively tells the operator the opposite — 'Silences a boot warning; only load-bearing if this site ever grows a mochi:defer island or signed image URLs' — with the variable left commented out, which makes 'unset in production' the likely state rather than a hypothetical. The consequence is as stated: every deploy or restart rotates the secret, so every captcha token already rendered into an open support page or an iframed newsletter widget decrypts to null and the visitor gets the deliberately-generic 'Verification failed — reload the page and try again', indistinguishable from a real failure; and a second replica could never verify the first's tokens. The replay note is also right that the default `store: 'memory'` (index.ts:57) drops burned nonces on restart, though with a rotating key those tokens are already unopenable, so the sqlite suggestion only matters once MOCHI_KEY is pinned. This is an availability/robustness defect plus wrong documentation, so the BUG severity is the right label.

Verified: `'/'` in packages/support/src/routes.ts:35 declares `serverProps` and the `send` action with no `rateLimit`, and `Mochi.serve()` in index.ts sets no global `rateLimit` and no `protection` gate, so `buildLimiter` (Mochi.ts:801-829) returns `null` for this pattern and `checkRouteLimit` is a no-op — there is genuinely no throttle on the route. Every sibling public route does have one (`/admin` routes.ts:85, `/newsletter/embed` newsletter/routes.ts:15, and both token GETs at 85/107), which makes the omission look like an oversight rather than a decision. A successful POST writes a row via `insertSubmission` (routes.ts:66) and enqueues an SMTP delivery to SUPPORT_TO (routes.ts:74), both unauthenticated. The captcha genuinely does not bound throughput: the token-minting GET is itself unlimited (`serverProps: () => ({ captcha: mintCaptcha() })`), the nonce store only stops reuse of one token rather than bulk minting, and `minAgeMs: 2000` is a per-token age check at verify time, which pipelining amortizes to nothing. I'd soften one number — at `DEFAULT_CAPTCHA_BITS = 19` the expected ~524k SHA-256 attempts is tens of milliseconds of native work per token, not 'a few milliseconds' (pow.ts documents ~1.36µs/attempt for the JS implementation), so a single host is plausibly in the tens-to-low-hundreds of submissions per second rather than 'hundreds', and it parallelizes trivially across cores or hosts. That does not change the conclusion: unbounded row insertion in `.db/support.sqlite`, unbounded jobs in the shared `queue.sqlite`, and unbounded mail to the one SMTP relay that the newsletter double-opt-in also depends on. MEDIUM is appropriate, and the suggested `skip: (req) => req.method !== 'POST'` mirrors the embed's existing shape exactly.

The code shape is exactly as described — `subExpiredIdsStmt.all(now)` at db.server.ts:326 selects on `status = 'pending' AND confirm_expires_at < ?` outside the transaction, and the transaction at 330-335 deletes by `id` alone without re-asserting the predicate — but the interleaving it depends on cannot occur in this app. `purgeExpiredPendingSubscribers` contains no `await` and no yield point of any kind: `bun:sqlite`'s `.all()` and `db.transaction(fn)()` are both synchronous, so the SELECT and the DELETEs execute inside one uninterrupted JS task. The purge's only caller is the cron handler in newsletter/jobs.server.ts:97, and Mochi's durable cron is in-process: `cronWorkHandler` (queue.ts:898-905) wraps `job.run(...)` through the ordinary bun-boss queue handler on the same event loop as the request handlers — there is no worker thread and no separate process. A visitor's `requestSubscription` re-arm, or the admin's `refreshConfirmToken`, therefore cannot land between the read and the delete, because the event loop is blocked for the whole function. The only configuration that would make the TOCTOU real is two OS processes sharing `.db/support.sqlite`, and nothing does: the queue and cron stores are deliberately separate files (index.ts:46-49), the app holds the single module-level `Database` handle, and the app is a one-container deployment (F5's own observation that a second replica is impossible cuts the same way here). So the described failure — a visitor seeing 'Check your inbox' while the purge silently deletes the row and the job logs 'vanished before its confirmation was sent' — is not reachable as written. Still worth the suggested hardening, since a predicate-less delete-by-id is one `await` or one extra process away from becoming a real bug, but it is not a present defect.
